title: Phi: Leveraging Pattern-based Hierarchical Sparsity for High-Efficiency Spiking Neural Networks
problem: Spiking Neural Network (SNN) accelerators exploit binary activation sparsity (0-1 spikes) to skip zero computations, but they ignore the structured distribution patterns present in spike activations, leaving significant compute savings unexploited. Existing designs treat each non-zero spike independently, incurring redundant runtime multiply-accumulate operations.
motivation: SNNs promise energy-efficient neuromorphic inference, but without exploiting inherent spike pattern structure, the achievable speedup and energy savings over conventional DNN accelerators are limited, stalling the transition of SNNs to practical deployment.
method: Phi introduces a two-level hierarchical sparsity framework for SNNs. Level 1 is vector-wise sparsity: spike activations are represented using a small set of pre-defined patterns selected offline via k-means clustering, enabling offline pre-computation of pattern-weight products so that most runtime multiply-accumulates are eliminated. Level 2 is element-wise sparsity: a highly sparse residual matrix (the complement of the Level 1 approximation) handles remaining activations, further reducing computation while preserving accuracy. A pattern-aware fine-tuning technique is applied to increase Level 2 sparsity. The Phi hardware architecture processes both levels on-the-fly, with dedicated datapaths for each sparsity tier.
key_novelty: A two-level hierarchical sparsity scheme that decomposes spike activations into pre-computable pattern vectors plus a highly sparse residual, enabling offline pattern-weight precomputation to eliminate the bulk of SNN runtime arithmetic.
contributions: Observation and characterization of structured pattern distributions in SNN binary spike activations.
Two-level (vector-wise + element-wise) hierarchical sparsity framework with k-means-based pattern selection and pattern-aware fine-tuning.
Phi hardware architecture with dedicated datapaths for both sparsity levels, processing activations on-the-fly.
3.45x speedup and 4.93x energy-efficiency improvement over state-of-the-art SNN accelerators.

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 4.93x improvement in energy efficiency over state-of-the-art SNN accelerators

limitations: The evaluation is limited to SNN workloads; applicability to conventional DNNs with binary activations is not discussed.
primary_theme: hierarchical pattern sparsity for spiking neural networks
